# Analysis plan: atac-differential-accessibility

Status: DRAFT

An analysis runs only after a person has read this file and approved it. Edit anything;
approval is what freezes it. After approval the plan is the record of intent -- change of
mind means a new analysis, not a quiet edit.

## Goal
Compare the two conditions (`b` vs `a`) across the ATAC-seq consensus peaks: test each
consensus peak for a difference in chromatin accessibility between condition `b` and condition
`a` (the reference level), and report the per-peak effect sizes and adjusted p-values. The design
has two replicates per condition (atac-a-r1, atac-a-r2; atac-b-r1, atac-b-r2).

## Inputs
Artifact types resolve through each sub-stage's OUTPUTS.tsv at execution time; the paths
below are what they resolve to today.

| Artifact type | Resolved from | Path |
|---|---|---|
| `counts_peaks` | 02_bioinformatics/atacseq_bulk/01_nfcore-atacseq-wrapper (native) | `02_bioinformatics/atacseq_bulk/01_nfcore-atacseq-wrapper/run/results/bwa/merged_library/macs2/narrow_peak/consensus/consensus_peaks.mLb.clN.featureCounts.txt` |
| `peaks_consensus` | 02_bioinformatics/atacseq_bulk/01_nfcore-atacseq-wrapper (native) | `02_bioinformatics/atacseq_bulk/01_nfcore-atacseq-wrapper/run/results/bwa/merged_library/macs2/narrow_peak/consensus/consensus_peaks.mLb.clN.bed` |
| `design` | 01_prepare_samplesheets (native) | `01_samplesheets/atacseq_bulk_design.csv` |

## Method
All steps run in one batch job, in the `gars-bio` conda environment (`source
_system/gars-env.sh`), using Python with pandas 3.0.5, pydeseq2 0.5.4 and matplotlib 3.11.1 —
all already in the environment's lockfile; nothing is installed. Inputs are opened read-only;
everything is written under `results/`.

1. **Resolve inputs.** At job start, re-run `_system/resolve_artifact.py --project
   projects/run-97e7f0ea --assay atacseq_bulk --type <T>` for `counts_peaks`,
   `peaks_consensus` and `design`, and use the paths it returns. If any fails to resolve, stop
   with that error.
2. **Load counts.** Read the featureCounts table (skip the `#` program line). Peak ID =
   `Geneid` (e.g. `Interval_1`); keep `Chr`, `Start`, `End`, `Length` as annotation. The
   four count columns are named `<group>_REP<replicate>.mLb.clN.sorted.bam`.
3. **Match samples to the design.** Map each count column to a design row by `group` and
   `replicate` (e.g. `atac-a_REP1…` → `atac-a-r1`, condition `a`). Stop with an error if any
   column fails to match exactly one design row, or any design row matches no column —
   no sample is dropped or guessed.
4. **Check the consensus peak set.** Confirm every peak ID in the counts table is in the
   consensus BED, and every BED peak is in the table (by ID or by chr/start/end). Record the
   peak count. If they disagree, stop with the error.
5. **Differential accessibility (DESeq2 model via pydeseq2).** Build a `DeseqDataSet` from the
   raw integer counts (peaks × samples), design `~condition`, reference level `a`. No
   pre-filtering of peaks, no prior normalisation — size factors are DESeq2's median-of-ratios
   over the consensus peaks. Fit with pydeseq2 defaults (parametric dispersion trend, Cook's
   distance outlier handling on its defaults). Run `DeseqStats` for contrast
   `["condition", "b", "a"]` with `alpha=0.05`, Wald test, Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment,
   default independent filtering. Apply `lfc_shrink` (apeGLM-style prior, as pydeseq2 provides
   it) and report shrunken log2FC beside the unshrunken value.
6. **Write the results table.** One row per consensus peak: `peak_id, chr, start, end,
   length, baseMean, log2FoldChange, log2FoldChange_shrunk, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj`, plus
   the normalised counts per sample, sorted by `padj` (NaN last). Also write the size factors
   and the normalised count matrix.
7. **Figures.**
   - MA plot: log10 mean normalised count vs shrunken log2FC, peaks with `padj < 0.05`
     highlighted.
   - Volcano plot: unshrunken log2FC vs −log10(`pvalue`), `padj < 0.05` highlighted.
   - Sample PCA: PC1 vs PC2 on variance-stabilised counts (pydeseq2 `vst`, blind), top 500
     most variable peaks, points coloured by condition and labelled by sample.
8. **Summary report.** Markdown listing input paths as resolved, sample-to-column mapping,
   peak count, size factors, the numbers of peaks with `padj < 0.05` and log2FC > 0 / < 0,
   software versions, and a note that with n = 2 per condition the test has limited power and
   dispersion estimates rely heavily on the fitted trend. No biological interpretation.

## Outputs
Types come from the closed vocabulary in _references/artifact_types.md.

`de_results` is defined as one row per gene, so the per-peak table is declared `table`; its
contents are described here.

| File | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `results/differential_accessibility_b_vs_a.tsv` | table | per-consensus-peak DESeq2 results for condition b vs a (step 6) |
| `results/normalized_counts.tsv` | table | median-of-ratios normalised counts, peaks × samples |
| `results/size_factors.tsv` | table | one size factor per sample |
| `results/ma_plot.png` | figure | MA plot, shrunken log2FC, padj < 0.05 highlighted |
| `results/volcano_plot.png` | figure | volcano plot, padj < 0.05 highlighted |
| `results/pca_samples.png` | figure | PCA of VST counts, top 500 variable peaks |
| `results/summary.md` | report | inputs, sample mapping, counts of significant peaks, versions, caveats |

## Execution
Runs: batch

One script, `scripts/differential_accessibility.py`, submitted through
`_system/executorlib.py submit` to the workspace's configured executor with 1 CPU and 8 GB
memory. Input is ~1,324 peaks × 4 samples, so expected wall time is under 5 minutes and total
output under 5 MB.

   consensus BED, and every BED peak is in the table (by ID or by chr/start/end). Record the

# GARS execution environment — the single definition of how to run a skill.
#
# Source this from every submit.sh:  source "$WS/_system/gars-env.sh"
#
# Why this file exists: the same ~10 lines of setup were previously copy-pasted into every
# submit.sh, in every project, for every sub-stage. They drifted — a salvaged script was found
# still referencing a vendored skills path that no longer existed.
#
# Why absolute paths rather than `conda activate`: activation would work, but stacking two
# environments needs conda's shell hook sourced inside every batch script, which is more moving
# parts and fails differently on nodes where the hook is absent. Absolute paths behave
# identically everywhere, which is what a Slurm script needs.
#
# Why this lives in the workspace and not in $HOME: a workspace is a copy of the template and
# the contracts treat it as self-contained, so copying a workspace carries its environment
# definition. It is versioned in git, so a change is a reviewable commit rather than an
# untracked edit to a home-directory script.

# --- root ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DO NOT substitute $HOME here. On this cluster $HOME (/gpfs/home/<user>) and the group work
# area (/gpfs/data/abl/home/<user>) are DIFFERENT directories with different inodes -- only some
# subtrees, such as install/, are shared via symlink. Using $HOME once pointed the container
# cache at an empty directory, which silently re-pulls all 26 images and looks like the cache
# "stopped working". Set GARS_ROOT explicitly (e.g. in ~/.bashrc) to the root that holds
# install/ -- there is deliberately no default, because any default is someone's home.
GARS_ROOT="${GARS_ROOT:?[gars-env] FATAL: set GARS_ROOT to the root holding install/ (see _references/environment.md)}"

# --- environments -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two, because nextflow and clawbio have conflicting c-ares constraints and cannot be solved
# together. See _references/environment.md.
GARS_BIO="${GARS_BIO:-$GARS_ROOT/install/miniconda_clean/envs/gars-bio}"   # clawbio, apptainer, squashfuse
GARS_NXF="${GARS_NXF:-$GARS_ROOT/install/miniconda_clean/envs/gars-nxf}"   # nextflow, openjdk 17

# Order matters. gars-nxf first so `java` resolves to its OpenJDK 17 rather than the system
# Java 1.8 — Nextflow locates Java via PATH, and refuses anything below 17.
export PATH="$GARS_NXF/bin:$GARS_BIO/bin:$PATH"
export JAVA_HOME="$GARS_NXF"

# --- caches -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared across projects: container images and the pinned pipeline are immutable and reusable.
export APPTAINER_CACHEDIR="${APPTAINER_CACHEDIR:-$GARS_ROOT/.apptainer_cache}"
export NXF_APPTAINER_CACHEDIR="$APPTAINER_CACHEDIR"
export NXF_HOME="${NXF_HOME:-$GARS_ROOT/.nextflow_gars}"
mkdir -p "$APPTAINER_CACHEDIR" "$NXF_HOME"

# --- resolved locations -------------------------------------------------------------------
export GARS_PY="$GARS_BIO/bin/python"

# The retired clawbio skills (decision 0029) are resolved for inspection only -- no sub-stage
# invokes them. The literal site-packages path embeds a Python version that changes on any
# environment rebuild, hence the runtime resolution. Empty if clawbio is absent; that is fine.
# `|| true` carries this file's own promise ("Empty if clawbio is absent; that is fine")
# through a caller's `set -e`: a failed command substitution in an assignment is FATAL under
# -e, and every generated submit.sh runs with -e. The cluster never saw it -- clawbio is
# always installed there; the first host without it (the demo's recording rig) died here
# silently, before the script's first echo.
GARS_SKILLS=$("$GARS_PY" -c "import clawbio, pathlib; print(pathlib.Path(clawbio.__file__).parent / 'skills')" 2>/dev/null || true)
export GARS_SKILLS

# GARS-authored wrappers, versioned in this workspace and ours to maintain (decision 0012).

content.content:
# Genomics Agentic Research System (GARS)

A workspace for running genomics research projects through dialogue with an LLM agent. The
filesystem is the architecture; the agent is the navigator. Built on the Interpretable Context
Methodology (ICM — Van Clief & McDermott, arXiv:2603.16021), with bioinformatics executed by
nf-core pipelines through GARS-authored
wrappers — every assay's sub-stage runs on one (decisions 0028-0031).

> **Scope of this file.** Orientation for *using* a GARS workspace. If you are developing GARS
> itself — editing contracts, docs or the template — the entry point is the `CLAUDE.md` at the
> root of the GARS source repository, not this one.

## Agent entry point

Before responding to any request: read `CONTEXT.md` for the stage map, then read the `CONTEXT.md`
of the stage the request maps to. Execute that contract literally.

- Its **Scope Boundaries** are binding. Do not read, search, or act outside them, however helpful
  the deviation would seem.
- Its **Response Format** templates are the only messages to send. Add no observations,
  suggestions, or offers of work. One exception: a direct user question may be answered from
  the workspace's own files, read-only, before restating the current wait point — the bounded
  voice rule in `_references/contract_standard.md`.
- If a step appears to need deviation, stop and ask. Never act first and report afterwards.

## Where things live

| Path | Holds | Layer |
|---|---|---|
| `CONTEXT.md` | stage map, how stages connect, directory ownership | L1 |
| `00_initialize_project/` … `03_custom_analysis/` | one contract per stage; the numbering is the order | L2 |
| `02_bioinformatics/<Assay ID>/<NN_name>/` | one contract per sub-stage of an assay | L2 |
| `_references/` | domain knowledge shared by every project — assay map, artifact vocabulary, config schema, runtime | L3 |
| `_templates/` | the stamps stages copy; `project/` is the shape of a new project | L3 |
| `_system/` | `gars-env.sh` (the execution environment), the stage helpers that compute deterministic artifacts, the index builder | L3 |
| `projects/` | the work: one directory per project, plus a generated `_index.md` | L4 |

Wrappers are **versioned here**, under `_system/wrappers/`, resolved as `$GARS_WRAPPERS`
(decision 0012); every sub-stage's Source in the assay map is `gars`. The retired ClawBio
skills remain installed with the `clawbio` package but no sub-stage uses them (decision 0029;
procedures deleted 2026-08-27). A sub-stage directory holds a `CONTEXT.md`, never a `.py`.

**Derived artifacts are computed by code, not written by you.** Samplesheets, design tables, the
project index and artifact resolution come from `_system/` scripts. A contract that names one is
telling you to run it and report what it returns — not to reproduce its work. The stage 00/01
helpers and the resolver need no conda environment; stage 02's skills do.

## Using this workspace

1. Clone the GARS repository; **this folder, `gars/`, is your workspace** — work here directly.
   `git pull` before starting a project to pick up fixes; `git checkout <tag>` to pin a release.
2. Tell the agent you want to start a new project → stage 00 creates `projects/<title>/` from
   `_templates/project/`, symlinks your raw data, and writes `files.csv` + `samples.csv` per assay.
3. **Fill in `00_data/<Assay ID>/samples.csv`** — one row per sample, so each experimental value
   is entered once; the header shows this assay's columns (ChIP-family assays add `control`).
   To analyse a subset, delete the other rows: stage 01 treats a sample with no
   row as excluded and leaves its raw data in place, so the choice is reversible.
4. `_config/` is already seeded — stage 00 filled every derivable value and marked the
   scientific decisions `<REQUIRED>`. Stage 02 completes those from menus (genome; contrast
   and formula, or peak type, per assay) and asks you to confirm before writing. Schema and rationale:
   `_references/config_schema.md`.
5. Run stages 01 → 02 → 03 in order, reading the output between each.

## State

There is no status file for the workspace. State is the filesystem — and every session boot
renders it for you: the SessionStart hook rebuilds `projects/_index.md` and prints
`_system/project_state.py`'s per-project catch-up (how far each assay got, which decisions
are unmade, the last HISTORY entries). Run it any time; it is a render, never a record:

| Question | Answered by |
|---|---|
| What projects exist, how far did each get? | `projects/_index.md` (generated — rebuild with `bash _system/build_projects_index.sh`) |
| Is a design complete? | `00_data/<Assay ID>/samples.csv` |

> root of the GARS source repository, not this one.

## Agent entry point

Before responding to any request: read `CONTEXT.md` for the stage map, then read the `CONTEXT.md`
of the stage the request maps to. Execute that contract literally.

- Its **Scope Boundaries** are binding. Do not read, search, or act outside them, however helpful
  the deviation would seem.
- Its **Response Format** templates are the only messages to send. Add no observations,

  the workspace's own files, read-only, before restating the current wait point — the bounded
  voice rule in `_references/contract_standard.md`.

| Path | Holds | Layer |
|---|---|---|
| `CONTEXT.md` | stage map, how stages connect, directory ownership | L1 |
| `00_initialize_project/` … `03_custom_analysis/` | one contract per stage; the numbering is the order | L2 |
| `02_bioinformatics/<Assay ID>/<NN_name>/` | one contract per sub-stage of an assay | L2 |

(decision 0012); every sub-stage's Source in the assay map is `gars`. The retired ClawBio
skills remain installed with the `clawbio` package but no sub-stage uses them (decision 0029;

                  fh, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
    return job_id


def _local_status(config_root, job_id):
    record = _local_jobs_dir(config_root) / ("%s.json" % job_id)
    if not record.is_file():
        return "FAILED"             # nothing here started that job; say so, never guess
    exit_file = Path(json.loads(record.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["exit_file"])
    if exit_file.is_file():
        return "COMPLETED" if exit_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip() == "0" else "FAILED"
    try:
        os.kill(int(job_id), 0)
        return "RUNNING"
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        pass
    return "FAILED"


def submit(config_root, script, descriptor=None):
    """Hand the generated script to the scheduler. Returns (job_id, detail-or-None)."""
    descriptor = descriptor if descriptor is not None else load(config_root)
    if descriptor.get("name") == "local":
        job_id = _local_submit(config_root, script)
        return (job_id, None) if job_id else (None, "the local backend printed no PID")
    argv = submit_argv(descriptor, script)
    if not argv:
        return None, "the descriptor names no submit_argv"
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(argv, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    except OSError as exc:
        return None, "cannot run %s: %s" % (argv[0], exc)
    out = (proc.stdout or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace")
    err = (proc.stderr or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace")
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        return None, "%s exited %d: %s" % (argv[0], proc.returncode, (err or out).strip())
    try:
        m = re.search(descriptor.get("job_id_regex") or r"(\d+)", out)
    except re.error as exc:
        return None, "job_id_regex does not compile: %s" % exc
    if not m:
        return None, "no job id in the submit output: %r" % out.strip()
    return m.group(1), None


def status(config_root, job_id, descriptor=None):
    """Ask after a job. Returns (state, detail-or-None); state is one of STATES."""
    descriptor = descriptor if descriptor is not None else load(config_root)
    if descriptor.get("name") == "local":
        return _local_status(config_root, job_id), None
    argv = status_argv(descriptor, job_id)
    if not argv:
        return None, "the descriptor names no status_argv"
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(argv, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    except OSError as exc:
        return None, "cannot run %s: %s" % (argv[0], exc)
    out = (proc.stdout or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace")
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        return None, "%s exited %d" % (argv[0], proc.returncode)
    raw = ""
    for line in out.splitlines():
        if line.strip():
            raw = line.strip()
            break
    # `CANCELLED by 1234` and `COMPLETED+` are the shapes sacct actually prints.
    token = raw.split()[0].rstrip("+").upper() if raw else ""
    mapped = (descriptor.get("status_map") or {}).get(token)
    if not mapped:
        return None, "unmapped backend state %r -- add it to status_map" % (token or raw)
    return mapped, None


# --- CLI ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def emit(result, code):
    json.dump(result, sys.stdout, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
    sys.stdout.write("\n")
    return code


def main(argv=None):
    # `--workspace` is accepted on either side of the subcommand: the contracts write it
    # after (`... submit --workspace <project> <script>`), a shell habit writes it before.
    common = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)
    common.add_argument("--workspace", default=argparse.SUPPRESS,
                        help="the project directory that owns _config/")
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="The workspace's batch executor (0039).",
                                     parents=[common])
    parser.set_defaults(workspace=".")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command")

    p_header = sub.add_parser("header", parents=[common],
                              help="print the generated submit.sh directives block")
    p_header.add_argument("--project", default="{project}")
    p_header.add_argument("--assay", default="{assay}")
    p_header.add_argument("--substage", default=".")
    for key in ("partition", "time", "cpus", "mem"):
        p_header.add_argument("--" + key, default=None)

    p_submit = sub.add_parser("submit", parents=[common],
                              help="submit a GENERATED submit.sh")
    p_submit.add_argument("script")

    p_status = sub.add_parser("status", parents=[common],
                              help="the state of a submitted job")
    p_status.add_argument("job_id")

    sub.add_parser("describe", parents=[common],
                   help="the resolved descriptor and any problems with it")

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if not args.command:
        parser.print_help()
        return EXIT_USAGE

    root = Path(args.workspace)
    descriptor = load(root)
    problems = validate(descriptor)
    result = {"command": args.command, "executor": descriptor.get("name"),
              "descriptor": str(descriptor_path(root)),
GARS_ROOT=
results
# The workspace's batch executor (decision 0039). Seeded by stage 00; edit it per site.
#
# Required, not optional in spirit: GARS submits real work to a managed scheduler and never
# runs it in the current process (decision 0027). This file says WHICH scheduler. Delete it
# and the built-in Slurm descriptor below is what you get, byte for byte -- so an existing
# cluster workspace behaves exactly as it always has.
#
# The shape is deliberately narrow -- scalars, one-level lists, one-level `key: value` maps.
# `_system/` is stdlib-only (decision 0011), so this is parsed by a small parser we own, not
# by a YAML library. Do not reach for anchors, multi-line scalars or nested lists.
#
# Three doors, and nothing else:
#   header   the directives block the generated submit.sh opens with
#   submit   the argv that hands that GENERATED script to the scheduler -> a job id
#   status   the argv that asks after it -> PENDING | RUNNING | COMPLETED | FAILED
#
# `submit_argv` runs the generated `submit.sh` and nothing else. It is not a place to add
# pipeline parameters, environment or wrapper logic: the audited parameter surface is
# `_config/<assay>.yaml`, and bypassing it is the one thing this file must never enable.

# The backend. `slurm` and `local` are built in; any other name means this file supplies the
# whole descriptor. (`local` runs the script detached on this machine and reports its PID --
# it is for testing the submit->status walk without a cluster, never a venue for analyses.)
name: slurm

# The directives block. Available placeholders, and only these:
#   {project} {assay} {substage} {partition} {time} {cpus} {mem}
# compute.partition / time / cpus / mem come from `_config/<assay>.yaml`.
directives:
  - "#SBATCH --job-name={project}-{assay}"
  - "#SBATCH --partition={partition}"
  - "#SBATCH --time={time}"
  - "#SBATCH --cpus-per-task={cpus}"
  - "#SBATCH --mem={mem}"
  - "#SBATCH --output={substage}/logs/slurm-%j.out"
  - "#SBATCH --error={substage}/logs/slurm-%j.err"

# How a script becomes a job. {script} is the generated submit.sh; it must appear.
submit_argv:
  - sbatch

# GARS-authored wrappers, versioned in this workspace and ours to maintain (decision 0012).
# Every sub-stage runs on one (decisions 0028-0031); the retired clawbio skills stay installed
# but uninvoked (decision 0029).
export GARS_WRAPPERS="${GARS_WRAPPERS:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/wrappers}"

# Pinned pipeline checkout. Cloned over the git protocol, because resolving a remote
# nf-core/rnaseq goes through the GitHub REST API, which is rate-limited to 60 requests/hour
# across this site's shared outbound IP.
export GARS_PIPELINES="${GARS_PIPELINES:-$GARS_ROOT/install/nf-core-pipelines}"
export GARS_REFS="${GARS_REFS:-$GARS_ROOT/install/refs}"

# --- fail fast ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A missing piece here becomes an obscure failure minutes into a scheduled job otherwise.
for _v in GARS_BIO GARS_NXF; do
    if [ -z "${!_v:-}" ] || [ ! -e "${!_v}" ]; then
        echo "[gars-env] FATAL: $_v is unset or missing (${!_v:-unset})" >&2
        echo "[gars-env] See _references/environment.md for the install procedure." >&2
        return 1 2>/dev/null || exit 1
    fi
done
unset _v

# A cache that exists but is empty is the dangerous case: runs succeed, slowly, re-pulling
# everything. Warn rather than fail -- a genuinely first run has an empty cache legitimately.
if [ -d "$APPTAINER_CACHEDIR" ] && [ -z "$(ls -A "$APPTAINER_CACHEDIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
    echo "[gars-env] NOTE: container cache $APPTAINER_CACHEDIR is empty -- images will be pulled." >&2
fi

echo "[gars-env] python=$("$GARS_PY" --version 2>&1) | nextflow=$(nextflow -v 2>&1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1) | apptainer=$(apptainer --version 2>&1 | awk '{print $3}')"
echo "[gars-env] skills=$GARS_SKILLS"
if [ -d "$GARS_WRAPPERS" ]; then
    echo "[gars-env] wrappers=$GARS_WRAPPERS ($(ls -1 "$GARS_WRAPPERS" 2>/dev/null | wc -l))"
fi
echo "[gars-env] cache=$APPTAINER_CACHEDIR ($(ls "$APPTAINER_CACHEDIR"/*.img 2>/dev/null | wc -l) images)"
results
OUTPUTS.tsv
STATUS
run

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Differential accessibility, condition b vs a, over the ATAC-seq consensus peaks.

Implements PLAN.md (approved) steps 1-8 of 03_custom_analysis/01_atac-differential-accessibility.
Inputs are read-only; every output lands in results/.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
import pydeseq2  # noqa: E402
from pydeseq2.dds import DeseqDataSet  # noqa: E402
from pydeseq2.default_inference import DefaultInference  # noqa: E402
from pydeseq2.ds import DeseqStats  # noqa: E402

ANALYSIS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
PROJECT = ANALYSIS.parent.parent
WORKSPACE = PROJECT.parent.parent
RESULTS = ANALYSIS / "results"
ASSAY = "atacseq_bulk"
ALPHA = 0.05
REF, ALT = "a", "b"


def fail(msg):
    sys.stderr.write("ERROR: %s\n" % msg)
    sys.exit(1)


# 1. Resolve inputs --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def resolve(artifact_type):
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, str(WORKSPACE / "_system" / "resolve_artifact.py"),
         "--project", str(PROJECT), "--assay", ASSAY, "--type", artifact_type],
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    try:
        out = json.loads(proc.stdout.decode("utf-8"))
    except ValueError:
        fail("resolve_artifact.py --type %s returned no JSON (exit %d): %s"
             % (artifact_type, proc.returncode, proc.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace")))
    if proc.returncode != 0 or not out.get("ok") or artifact_type not in out.get("resolved", {}):
        fail("cannot resolve %s: %s" % (artifact_type, json.dumps(out, indent=2)))
    return PROJECT / out["resolved"][artifact_type]["resolved"]


paths = {t: resolve(t) for t in ("counts_peaks", "peaks_consensus", "design")}
for t, p in paths.items():
    print("[resolve] %s -> %s" % (t, p))
    if not p.is_file():
        fail("%s resolved to %s, which is not a file" % (t, p))

# 2. Load counts -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
fc = pd.read_csv(paths["counts_peaks"], sep="\t", comment="#")
annot_cols = ["Geneid", "Chr", "Start", "End", "Strand", "Length"]
missing = [c for c in annot_cols if c not in fc.columns]
if missing:
    fail("featureCounts table lacks columns %s" % missing)
fc = fc.set_index("Geneid")
fc.index.name = "peak_id"
annotation = fc[["Chr", "Start", "End", "Length"]].rename(
    columns={"Chr": "chr", "Start": "start", "End": "end", "Length": "length"})
count_cols = [c for c in fc.columns if c not in annot_cols]

# 3. Match samples to the design --------------------------------------------------------------
design = pd.read_csv(paths["design"], dtype=str)
col_re = re.compile(r"^(?P<group>.+)_REP(?P<rep>\d+)\.mLb\.clN\.sorted\.bam$")
mapping = {}
for col in count_cols:
    m = col_re.match(col)
    if not m:
        fail("count column %r does not match <group>_REP<replicate>.mLb.clN.sorted.bam" % col)
    hits = design[(design["group"] == m.group("group"))
                  & (design["replicate"].astype(int) == int(m.group("rep")))]
    if len(hits) != 1:
        fail("count column %r matches %d design rows (expected exactly 1)" % (col, len(hits)))
    mapping[col] = hits.iloc[0]["sample_id"]
unmatched = sorted(set(design["sample_id"]) - set(mapping.values()))
if unmatched:
    fail("design rows with no count column: %s" % unmatched)
if len(set(mapping.values())) != len(mapping):
    fail("two count columns map to the same design row: %s" % mapping)

counts = fc[count_cols].rename(columns=mapping)
samples = list(counts.columns)
metadata = design.set_index("sample_id").loc[samples, ["condition", "group", "replicate"]]
if sorted(metadata["condition"].unique()) != sorted([REF, ALT]):
    fail("design conditions are %s, expected exactly %s and %s"
         % (sorted(metadata["condition"].unique()), REF, ALT))
metadata["condition"] = pd.Categorical(metadata["condition"], categories=[REF, ALT])

# 4. Check the consensus peak set -------------------------------------------------------------
bed = pd.read_csv(paths["peaks_consensus"], sep="\t", header=None, comment="#")
if bed.shape[1] < 4:
    fail("consensus BED has %d columns; a peak name column (4) is required" % bed.shape[1])
bed_ids = set(bed[3].astype(str))
count_ids = set(counts.index.astype(str))
if bed_ids != count_ids or len(bed) != len(counts):
    fail("consensus BED and counts table disagree: %d BED peaks, %d counted peaks, "
         "%d only in BED, %d only in counts"
         % (len(bed), len(counts), len(bed_ids - count_ids), len(count_ids - bed_ids)))
n_peaks = len(counts)
print("[check] %d consensus peaks, all counted" % n_peaks)

# 5. Differential accessibility --------------------------------------------------------------
RESULTS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
inference = DefaultInference(n_cpus=1)
dds = DeseqDataSet(counts=counts.T.astype(int), metadata=metadata, design="~condition",
                   inference=inference, quiet=True)
dds.deseq2()

ds = DeseqStats(dds, contrast=["condition", ALT, REF], alpha=ALPHA, inference=inference,
                quiet=True)
ds.summary()
res = ds.results_df.copy()

lfc_cols = list(dds.varm["LFC"].columns)
coeff = [c for c in lfc_cols if c.startswith("condition") and c.endswith(ALT)]
if len(coeff) != 1:
    fail("cannot identify the condition coefficient among %s" % lfc_cols)
ds.lfc_shrink(coeff=coeff[0])
res["log2FoldChange_shrunk"] = ds.results_df["log2FoldChange"]

# 6. Results tables ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
normed = pd.DataFrame(dds.layers["normed_counts"], index=dds.obs_names,
                      columns=dds.var_names).T
normed.index.name = "peak_id"
size_factors = pd.DataFrame({"sample_id": dds.obs_names,
                             "size_factor": np.asarray(dds.obs["size_factors"])})

table = annotation.join(res[["baseMean", "log2FoldChange", "log2FoldChange_shrunk", "lfcSE",
                             "stat", "pvalue", "padj"]])
table = table.join(normed.add_prefix("norm_"))
table = table.sort_values("padj", na_position="last")
table.to_csv(RESULTS / "differential_accessibility_b_vs_a.tsv", sep="\t")
normed.to_csv(RESULTS / "normalized_counts.tsv", sep="\t")
size_factors.to_csv(RESULTS / "size_factors.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)

sig = table["padj"] < ALPHA
n_sig = int(sig.sum())
n_up = int((sig & (table["log2FoldChange"] > 0)).sum())
n_down = int((sig & (table["log2FoldChange"] < 0)).sum())

# 7. Figures -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
GREY, HIGHLIGHT = "#9e9e9e", "#c0392b"

plotted = table[table["baseMean"] > 0]
psig = plotted["padj"] < ALPHA
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
ax.scatter(np.log10(plotted.loc[~psig, "baseMean"]), plotted.loc[~psig, "log2FoldChange_shrunk"],
           s=6, c=GREY, alpha=0.6, linewidths=0, label="padj >= %.2f or NA" % ALPHA)
ax.scatter(np.log10(plotted.loc[psig, "baseMean"]), plotted.loc[psig, "log2FoldChange_shrunk"],
           s=8, c=HIGHLIGHT, linewidths=0, label="padj < %.2f (n=%d)" % (ALPHA, int(psig.sum())))
ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel("log10 mean normalised count")
ax.set_ylabel("shrunken log2 fold change (b vs a)")
ax.set_title("MA plot: consensus peaks, b vs a")
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(RESULTS / "ma_plot.png", dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

vol = table.dropna(subset=["pvalue"])
vsig = vol["padj"] < ALPHA
neglog = -np.log10(vol["pvalue"].clip(lower=np.finfo(float).tiny))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
ax.scatter(vol.loc[~vsig, "log2FoldChange"], neglog[~vsig], s=6, c=GREY, alpha=0.6,
           linewidths=0, label="padj >= %.2f or NA" % ALPHA)
ax.scatter(vol.loc[vsig, "log2FoldChange"], neglog[vsig], s=8, c=HIGHLIGHT, linewidths=0,
           label="padj < %.2f (n=%d)" % (ALPHA, int(vsig.sum())))
ax.set_xlabel("log2 fold change (b vs a)")
ax.set_ylabel("-log10 p-value")
ax.set_title("Volcano plot: consensus peaks, b vs a")
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(RESULTS / "volcano_plot.png", dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

# Blind VST on a separate dataset, so the fitted model above is untouched.
dds_vst = DeseqDataSet(counts=counts.T.astype(int), metadata=metadata, design="~condition",
                       inference=inference, quiet=True)
dds_vst.vst(use_design=False)
vst = pd.DataFrame(dds_vst.layers["vst_counts"], index=dds_vst.obs_names,
                   columns=dds_vst.var_names)
top = vst.var(axis=0).sort_values(ascending=False).index[:500]
x = vst[top].values
x = x - x.mean(axis=0)
u, s, _ = np.linalg.svd(x, full_matrices=False)
pcs = u * s
var_explained = s ** 2 / np.sum(s ** 2)
colors = {REF: "#2c7fb8", ALT: "#d95f0e"}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.5, 5))
for cond in (REF, ALT):
    idx = [i for i, sm in enumerate(vst.index) if metadata.loc[sm, "condition"] == cond]
    ax.scatter(pcs[idx, 0], pcs[idx, 1], s=60, c=colors[cond], label="condition %s" % cond)
for i, sm in enumerate(vst.index):
    ax.annotate(sm, (pcs[i, 0], pcs[i, 1]), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(5, 5),
                fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlabel("PC1 (%.1f%%)" % (100 * var_explained[0]))
ax.set_ylabel("PC2 (%.1f%%)" % (100 * var_explained[1]))
ax.set_title("PCA, blind VST, top %d variable peaks" % len(top))
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(RESULTS / "pca_samples.png", dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

# 8. Summary report ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
lines = [
    "# Differential accessibility: condition b vs a",
    "",
    "Plan: `03_custom_analysis/01_atac-differential-accessibility/PLAN.md`",
    "",
    "## Inputs (as resolved)",
    "",
    "| Artifact type | Path |",
    "|---|---|",
]
lines += ["| `%s` | `%s` |" % (t, os.path.relpath(str(p), str(PROJECT))) for t, p in paths.items()]
lines += ["", "## Sample mapping", "", "| Count column | sample_id | condition |", "|---|---|---|"]
lines += ["| `%s` | %s | %s |" % (c, sm, metadata.loc[sm, "condition"])
          for c, sm in mapping.items()]
lines += ["", "## Size factors", "", "| sample_id | size factor |", "|---|---|"]
lines += ["| %s | %.4f |" % (r.sample_id, r.size_factor) for r in size_factors.itertuples()]
lines += [
    "",
    "## Counts",
    "",
    "| | n |",
    "|---|---|",
    "| consensus peaks tested | %d |" % n_peaks,
    "| padj < %.2f | %d |" % (ALPHA, n_sig),
    "| padj < %.2f, log2FC > 0 (higher in b) | %d |" % (ALPHA, n_up),
    "| padj < %.2f, log2FC < 0 (higher in a) | %d |" % (ALPHA, n_down),
    "| padj NA (independent filtering / outliers) | %d |" % int(table["padj"].isna().sum()),
    "",
    "Model: pydeseq2 `~condition`, reference level `a`, Wald test, Benjamini-Hochberg, "
    "alpha = %.2f; shrunken log2FC from `lfc_shrink(coeff=%r)`." % (ALPHA, coeff[0]),
    "",
    "## Software",
    "",
    "- python %s" % sys.version.split()[0],
    "- pydeseq2 %s" % pydeseq2.__version__,
    "- pandas %s" % pd.__version__,
    "- numpy %s" % np.__version__,
    "- matplotlib %s" % matplotlib.__version__,
    "",
    "## Caveats",
    "",
    "With n = 2 replicates per condition the test has limited power, and per-peak dispersion "
    "estimates rely heavily on the fitted dispersion trend.",
    "",
]
(RESULTS / "summary.md").write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
print("[done] %d peaks, %d with padj < %.2f" % (n_peaks, n_sig, ALPHA))

Implements PLAN.md (approved) steps 1-8 of 03_custom_analysis/01_atac-differential-accessibility.
Inputs are read-only; every output lands in results/.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
import pydeseq2  # noqa: E402
from pydeseq2.dds import DeseqDataSet  # noqa: E402
from pydeseq2.default_inference import DefaultInference  # noqa: E402
from pydeseq2.ds import DeseqStats  # noqa: E402

ANALYSIS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
PROJECT = ANALYSIS.parent.parent
WORKSPACE = PROJECT.parent.parent
RESULTS = ANALYSIS / "results"
ASSAY = "atacseq_bulk"
ALPHA = 0.05
REF, ALT = "a", "b"


def fail(msg):
    sys.stderr.write("ERROR: %s\n" % msg)
    sys.exit(1)


# 1. Resolve inputs --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def resolve(artifact_type):
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, str(WORKSPACE / "_system" / "resolve_artifact.py"),
         "--project", str(PROJECT), "--assay", ASSAY, "--type", artifact_type],
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    try:
        out = json.loads(proc.stdout.decode("utf-8"))
    except ValueError:
        fail("resolve_artifact.py --type %s returned no JSON (exit %d): %s"
             % (artifact_type, proc.returncode, proc.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace")))
    if proc.returncode != 0 or not out.get("ok") or artifact_type not in out.get("resolved", {}):
        fail("cannot resolve %s: %s" % (artifact_type, json.dumps(out, indent=2)))
    return PROJECT / out["resolved"][artifact_type]["resolved"]


paths = {t: resolve(t) for t in ("counts_peaks", "peaks_consensus", "design")}
for t, p in paths.items():
    print("[resolve] %s -> %s" % (t, p))
    if not p.is_file():
        fail("%s resolved to %s, which is not a file" % (t, p))

# 2. Load counts -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
fc = pd.read_csv(paths["counts_peaks"], sep="\t", comment="#")
annot_cols = ["Geneid", "Chr", "Start", "End", "Strand", "Length"]
missing = [c for c in annot_cols if c not in fc.columns]
if missing:
    fail("featureCounts table lacks columns %s" % missing)
fc = fc.set_index("Geneid")
fc.index.name = "peak_id"
annotation = fc[["Chr", "Start", "End", "Length"]].rename(
    columns={"Chr": "chr", "Start": "start", "End": "end", "Length": "length"})
count_cols = [c for c in fc.columns if c not in annot_cols]

# 3. Match samples to the design --------------------------------------------------------------
design = pd.read_csv(paths["design"], dtype=str)
col_re = re.compile(r"^(?P<group>.+)_REP(?P<rep>\d+)\.mLb\.clN\.sorted\.bam$")
mapping = {}
for col in count_cols:
    m = col_re.match(col)
    if not m:
        fail("count column %r does not match <group>_REP<replicate>.mLb.clN.sorted.bam" % col)
    hits = design[(design["group"] == m.group("group"))
                  & (design["replicate"].astype(int) == int(m.group("rep")))]
    if len(hits) != 1:
        fail("count column %r matches %d design rows (expected exactly 1)" % (col, len(hits)))
    mapping[col] = hits.iloc[0]["sample_id"]
unmatched = sorted(set(design["sample_id"]) - set(mapping.values()))
if unmatched:
    fail("design rows with no count column: %s" % unmatched)
if len(set(mapping.values())) != len(mapping):
    fail("two count columns map to the same design row: %s" % mapping)

counts = fc[count_cols].rename(columns=mapping)
samples = list(counts.columns)
metadata = design.set_index("sample_id").loc[samples, ["condition", "group", "replicate"]]
if sorted(metadata["condition"].unique()) != sorted([REF, ALT]):
    fail("design conditions are %s, expected exactly %s and %s"
         % (sorted(metadata["condition"].unique()), REF, ALT))
metadata["condition"] = pd.Categorical(metadata["condition"], categories=[REF, ALT])

# 4. Check the consensus peak set -------------------------------------------------------------
bed = pd.read_csv(paths["peaks_consensus"], sep="\t", header=None, comment="#")
if bed.shape[1] < 4:
    fail("consensus BED has %d columns; a peak name column (4) is required" % bed.shape[1])
bed_ids = set(bed[3].astype(str))
count_ids = set(counts.index.astype(str))
if bed_ids != count_ids or len(bed) != len(counts):
    fail("consensus BED and counts table disagree: %d BED peaks, %d counted peaks, "
         "%d only in BED, %d only in counts"
         % (len(bed), len(counts), len(bed_ids - count_ids), len(count_ids - bed_ids)))
n_peaks = len(counts)
print("[check] %d consensus peaks, all counted" % n_peaks)

# 5. Differential accessibility --------------------------------------------------------------
RESULTS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
inference = DefaultInference(n_cpus=1)
dds = DeseqDataSet(counts=counts.T.astype(int), metadata=metadata, design="~condition",
                   inference=inference, quiet=True)
dds.deseq2()

ds = DeseqStats(dds, contrast=["condition", ALT, REF], alpha=ALPHA, inference=inference,
                quiet=True)
ds.summary()
res = ds.results_df.copy()

lfc_cols = list(dds.varm["LFC"].columns)
coeff = [c for c in lfc_cols if c.startswith("condition") and c.endswith(ALT)]
if len(coeff) != 1:
    fail("cannot identify the condition coefficient among %s" % lfc_cols)
ds.lfc_shrink(coeff=coeff[0])
res["log2FoldChange_shrunk"] = ds.results_df["log2FoldChange"]

# 6. Results tables ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
normed = pd.DataFrame(dds.layers["normed_counts"], index=dds.obs_names,
                      columns=dds.var_names).T
normed.index.name = "peak_id"
size_factors = pd.DataFrame({"sample_id": dds.obs_names,
                             "size_factor": np.asarray(dds.obs["size_factors"])})

table = annotation.join(res[["baseMean", "log2FoldChange", "log2FoldChange_shrunk", "lfcSE",
                             "stat", "pvalue", "padj"]])
table = table.join(normed.add_prefix("norm_"))
table = table.sort_values("padj", na_position="last")
table.to_csv(RESULTS / "differential_accessibility_b_vs_a.tsv", sep="\t")
normed.to_csv(RESULTS / "normalized_counts.tsv", sep="\t")
size_factors.to_csv(RESULTS / "size_factors.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)

sig = table["padj"] < ALPHA
n_sig = int(sig.sum())
n_up = int((sig & (table["log2FoldChange"] > 0)).sum())
n_down = int((sig & (table["log2FoldChange"] < 0)).sum())

# 7. Figures -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
GREY, HIGHLIGHT = "#9e9e9e", "#c0392b"

plotted = table[table["baseMean"] > 0]
psig = plotted["padj"] < ALPHA
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
ax.scatter(np.log10(plotted.loc[~psig, "baseMean"]), plotted.loc[~psig, "log2FoldChange_shrunk"],
           s=6, c=GREY, alpha=0.6, linewidths=0, label="padj >= %.2f or NA" % ALPHA)
ax.scatter(np.log10(plotted.loc[psig, "baseMean"]), plotted.loc[psig, "log2FoldChange_shrunk"],
           s=8, c=HIGHLIGHT, linewidths=0, label="padj < %.2f (n=%d)" % (ALPHA, int(psig.sum())))
ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel("log10 mean normalised count")
ax.set_ylabel("shrunken log2 fold change (b vs a)")
ax.set_title("MA plot: consensus peaks, b vs a")
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(RESULTS / "ma_plot.png", dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

vol = table.dropna(subset=["pvalue"])
vsig = vol["padj"] < ALPHA
neglog = -np.log10(vol["pvalue"].clip(lower=np.finfo(float).tiny))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
ax.scatter(vol.loc[~vsig, "log2FoldChange"], neglog[~vsig], s=6, c=GREY, alpha=0.6,
           linewidths=0, label="padj >= %.2f or NA" % ALPHA)
ax.scatter(vol.loc[vsig, "log2FoldChange"], neglog[vsig], s=8, c=HIGHLIGHT, linewidths=0,
           label="padj < %.2f (n=%d)" % (ALPHA, int(vsig.sum())))
ax.set_xlabel("log2 fold change (b vs a)")
ax.set_ylabel("-log10 p-value")
ax.set_title("Volcano plot: consensus peaks, b vs a")
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(RESULTS / "volcano_plot.png", dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

# Blind VST on a separate dataset, so the fitted model above is untouched.
dds_vst = DeseqDataSet(counts=counts.T.astype(int), metadata=metadata, design="~condition",
                       inference=inference, quiet=True)
dds_vst.vst(use_design=False)
vst = pd.DataFrame(dds_vst.layers["vst_counts"], index=dds_vst.obs_names,
                   columns=dds_vst.var_names)
top = vst.var(axis=0).sort_values(ascending=False).index[:500]
x = vst[top].values
x = x - x.mean(axis=0)
u, s, _ = np.linalg.svd(x, full_matrices=False)
pcs = u * s
var_explained = s ** 2 / np.sum(s ** 2)
colors = {REF: "#2c7fb8", ALT: "#d95f0e"}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.5, 5))
for cond in (REF, ALT):
    idx = [i for i, sm in enumerate(vst.index) if metadata.loc[sm, "condition"] == cond]
    ax.scatter(pcs[idx, 0], pcs[idx, 1], s=60, c=colors[cond], label="condition %s" % cond)
for i, sm in enumerate(vst.index):
    ax.annotate(sm, (pcs[i, 0], pcs[i, 1]), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(5, 5),
                fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlabel("PC1 (%.1f%%)" % (100 * var_explained[0]))
ax.set_ylabel("PC2 (%.1f%%)" % (100 * var_explained[1]))
ax.set_title("PCA, blind VST, top %d variable peaks" % len(top))
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(RESULTS / "pca_samples.png", dpi=150)

lines = [

    "Plan: `03_custom_analysis/01_atac-differential-accessibility/PLAN.md`",
    "",
    "## Inputs (as resolved)",
    "",
    "| Artifact type | Path |",
    "|---|---|",
]
lines += ["| `%s` | `%s` |" % (t, os.path.relpath(str(p), str(PROJECT))) for t, p in paths.items()]
lines += ["", "## Sample mapping", "", "| Count column | sample_id | condition |", "|---|---|---|"]
lines += ["| `%s` | %s | %s |" % (c, sm, metadata.loc[sm, "condition"])
          for c, sm in mapping.items()]
lines += ["", "## Size factors", "", "| sample_id | size factor |", "|---|---|"]
lines += ["| %s | %.4f |" % (r.sample_id, r.size_factor) for r in size_factors.itertuples()]
lines += [
    "",
    "## Counts",
    "",
    "| | n |",
    "|---|---|",
    "| consensus peaks tested | %d |" % n_peaks,
    "| padj < %.2f | %d |" % (ALPHA, n_sig),
    "| padj < %.2f, log2FC > 0 (higher in b) | %d |" % (ALPHA, n_up),

    "Model: pydeseq2 `~condition`, reference level `a`, Wald test, Benjamini-Hochberg, "
    "alpha = %.2f; shrunken log2FC from `lfc_shrink(coeff=%r)`." % (ALPHA, coeff[0]),
    "",
    "## Software",
    "",
    "- python %s" % sys.version.split()[0],
    "- pydeseq2 %s" % pydeseq2.__version__,
    "- pandas %s" % pd.__version__,
    "- numpy %s" % np.__version__,
    "- matplotlib %s" % matplotlib.__version__,
    "",
    "## Caveats",
    "",
    "With n = 2 replicates per condition the test has limited power, and per-peak dispersion "
    "estimates rely heavily on the fitted dispersion trend.",
    "",
]
(RESULTS / "summary.md").write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
print("[done] %d peaks, %d with padj < %.2f" % (n_peaks, n_sig, ALPHA))

lines += ["", "## Sample mapping", "", "| Count column | sample_id | condition |", "|---|---|---|"]
lines += ["| `%s` | %s | %s |" % (c, sm, metadata.loc[sm, "condition"])

lines += ["", "## Size factors", "", "| sample_id | size factor |", "|---|---|"]
lines += ["| %s | %.4f |" % (r.sample_id, r.size_factor) for r in size_factors.itertuples()]
lines += [
    "",
    "## Counts",
    "",
    "| | n |",
    "|---|---|",
    "| consensus peaks tested | %d |" % n_peaks,
    "| padj < %.2f | %d |" % (ALPHA, n_sig),

    "| padj < %.2f, log2FC < 0 (higher in a) | %d |" % (ALPHA, n_down),
    "| padj NA (independent filtering / outliers) | %d |" % int(table["padj"].isna().sum()),
    "",
    "Model: pydeseq2 `~condition`, reference level `a`, Wald test, Benjamini-Hochberg, "
    "alpha = %.2f; shrunken log2FC from `lfc_shrink(coeff=%r)`." % (ALPHA, coeff[0]),
    "",
    "## Software",
    "",
    "- python %s" % sys.version.split()[0],
    "- pydeseq2 %s" % pydeseq2.__version__,
    "- pandas %s" % pd.__version__,
    "- numpy %s" % np.__version__,
    "- matplotlib %s" % matplotlib.__version__,
    "",
    "## Caveats",
    "",
    "With n = 2 replicates per condition the test has limited power, and per-peak dispersion "
    "estimates rely heavily on the fitted dispersion trend.",
    "",
]
(RESULTS / "summary.md").write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
print("[done] %d peaks, %d with padj < %.2f" % (n_peaks, n_sig, ALPHA))
